title: The Third Architect: Dormal, the Dead Men's Drawings, and the Finishing of Buenos Aires
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: From the Meuse to the Paraná

stops.name: Liège, the birth on the coal river
stops.date_confidence: Year attested and agreed by every source that gives one, including the Argentine provincial legislative heritage report ('Nació en 1846 en Lieja') and the plaque cast for him in 1909, which reads 1846-1924. No civil birth act was located and no day or month is on record, so the date defaults to 1 January. The coordinate is the Liège city centre, used as a placeholder: the street of the birth is unknown.
stops.campa: A son is born at Liège in 1846, in the province where the Meuse turns north and where coal and ironwork have already made the town a place for engineers. No civil act naming the day has been found, and Liège keeps no monument to him. The family name he carries across an ocean is Dormal Godet, and Argentine paperwork will shorten him to Julio for the next seventy-eight years. Of the first twenty years nothing survives but what the Belgian schools taught him: mathematics, iron, the calculation of loads.
suggested_refs: Belgian civil registration for Liège, 1846, not yet consulted for the Dormal Godet birth act
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10, heritage report on the Estación Mar del Plata Sud (PDF)

stops.name: Place du 20-Août, the engineering course
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The University of Liège training is reported by Robert Hodge's 1979 study in The Americas, summarised through Cambridge Core, and by the provincial legislative report ('en cuya universidad cursó los estudios de ingeniería'). No matriculation record or diploma has been produced, and 1863 is chosen only to order the segment against an 1868 departure. The coordinate is corrected: a working value of 50.6437, 5.5729 sat about 500 m north-west of any university block; Nominatim gives Place du Vingt Août at 50.63978, 5.57586.
stops.campa: He follows the engineering course at the university on the Place du 20-Août, where an old Jesuit college has become the province's school of science. His matriculation has never been produced, and the registers of the Université de Liège have not been searched for it by anyone who writes about him. In Buenos Aires he will be called arquitecto and ingeniero in the same breath for fifty years, and when a plaque is finally cast for him both words are on it, in that order, with a hyphen holding them together.
suggested_refs: Matriculation registers of the Université de Liège for the 1860s
sources: Robert Hodge, 'The Construction of the Teatro Colón', The Americas (1979), via https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/americas/article/construction-of-the-teatro-colon/55098791BEBA8FCD22969773DA708C6F
Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: Paris, the school that cannot be named
stops.date_confidence: Genuine and unresolved contradiction, carried open. The provincial legislative report puts him at the École des Beaux-Arts under Trélat, Chabat, Gosicher and Viollet-le-Duc; the Buenos Aires city heritage page for Florida 466 and the weboeba catalogue put him at the École centrale des arts et manufactures; a third strand names the Polytechnique. No roll, no diploma and no dated inscription has been located for any of the three. 1866 orders the segment only. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Paris pin.
stops.campa: He goes to Paris to finish, and which school takes him is a question no two sources answer the same way. An Argentine legislative report puts him under Trélat, Chabat, Gosicher and Viollet-le-Duc at the Beaux-Arts. A Buenos Aires heritage page and a Belgian catalogue put him at the École centrale des arts et manufactures, which trains engineers and not architects at all. Nobody has produced a roll or a diploma for either, and a third strand of the tradition sends him to the Polytechnique instead. He leaves Paris carrying the manner of both.
suggested_refs: Registers of the École des Beaux-Arts and the École centrale des arts et manufactures, Paris, 1860s
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: Puerto Ruiz, the factory for essence of beef
stops.date_confidence: Arrival attested but its year contested: the legislative report and Hodge give 1868, the Buenos Aires city heritage page gives 1869, and the Belgian embassy at the 2024 centenary said 1870. The meat-extract commission at Gualeguay is attested; the specific placement at the river port of Puerto Ruiz is an inference and is not in the legislative PDF, which says only 'una fábrica de extractos de carne en Gualeguay'. Coordinate corrected to Nominatim's Puerto Ruiz, -33.22119, -59.36412; a working value of -33.35, -59.4667 lay about 17 km out in open country.
stops.campa: At about twenty-two he crosses the Atlantic under contract, not as an architect but as an engineer, to raise a plant for extracting essence of beef in the river country of Entre Ríos near Gualeguay. Argentina in these years kills cattle for the hide and burns the rest; extract is the answer Europe wants and the capital is European. The venture fails. He is left on the Paraná delta with a trade nobody nearby needs, and no particular reason to go home.
suggested_refs: Company records of the Gualeguay meat-extract works, 1868-1870, not located
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8
Robert Hodge, 'The Construction of the Teatro Colón', The Americas (1979)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the office that stays open fifty-four years
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the legislative report ('en 1870 se afincó en la ciudad de Buenos Aires donde estableció su estudio de arquitectura') and independently by the Belgian embassy's minister-counsellor Francis Sobry at the 2024 centenary. The exact street address of the office is unknown and the coordinate is the general microcentro pin. The non-naturalisation is attested by the arquitectos-franceses blog and contradicted by the embassy remarks of 2024, which called him a naturalised Argentine; the contradiction is left open.
stops.campa: The French minister plenipotentiary in Buenos Aires tells him to come down to the capital, and he comes. In 1870 he opens an architecture office in the old centre. It does not close for fifty-four years. What street it stood on nobody has recorded. He never takes Argentine citizenship, says the survey that put a caption on his house; the Belgian embassy, speaking at the centenary of his death, called him a naturalised Argentine. The two statements sit side by side and neither has been withdrawn.
stops.quote: El arquitecto Jules Dormal falleció aquí el 22 de Marzo de 1924 y si bien nunca adoptó la ciudadanía argentina residió en nuestro país por más de cincuenta años donde realizó muchísimas obras.
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires professional directories of the 1870s, for the address of the Dormal studio
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

segments.name: Palermo, and the Circle of the Presidents

stops.name: Casa de Gobierno, the friendship with two presidents
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. Hodge (1979) calls him 'a close friend of Sarmiento and Avellaneda' and the provincial legislative report says the French minister's introduction won him their friendship. No letter, minute or diary entry recording any meeting has been located, and Sarmiento's own file carries no mention of Dormal. The date orders the segment. The coordinate is the seat of the national executive, inherited byte-identical from the corpus Casa Rosada pin, and stands for the network, not for an attested encounter.
stops.campa: Two presidents take him up. Domingo Faustino Sarmiento, who wants the country dressed in stone and trees and schoolhouses, and Nicolás Avellaneda after him, admit the young Belgian to the circle where public work is handed out. Every account of his career reports the friendship and not one of them produces a letter, a minute, or a line in either president's papers. What is documented is the consequence. From 1874 onward the commissions come from the state, and they keep coming for thirty years.
suggested_refs: Correspondence of Sarmiento and of Avellaneda, searched for Dormal without result
sources: Robert Hodge, 'The Construction of the Teatro Colón', The Americas (1979)
Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: Parque Tres de Febrero, the second prize
stops.date_confidence: The competition and Dormal's second place are reported by Daniel Schávelzon's study of the Parque Tres de Febrero competition as relayed in the research pool, tagged as reconstruction there. The legislative report's claim that Dormal made the park's first layout is contradicted by es.wikipedia's Parque Tres de Febrero, which gives the plan to Nicolás Descalzi, the engineering charge to Jordán Wysocki, and the won competition to Methfessel and Börmel, whose scheme 'no se concretó por sus costos elevados'. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Palermo park pin.
stops.campa: The government turns the confiscated Palermo ground of Rosas into a public park and calls a competition for it. The Swiss pair Methfessel and Börmel win; Dormal takes second. Neither scheme is built, both costing more than the treasury holds, and the execution passes to the Polish engineer Jordán Czeslaw Wysocki over a plan by Nicolás Descalzi. What Dormal is given is the entrance and the avenue. A provincial heritage report written a century later hands him the first layout of the whole park instead.
suggested_refs: Daniel Schávelzon on the 1874 Parque Tres de Febrero competition
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: Portones de Palermo, the gates and the avenue
stops.date_confidence: Inauguration date attested by the legislative report ('siendo inaugurado el 11 de noviembre de 1875'), with the park's twenty-five hectares, lakes, Rosedal and gazebo. Dormal's authorship of the gates and the main avenue rests on es.wikipedia's Parque Tres de Febrero and on the Wikimedia Commons category for him, which carries a Portones de Palermo photograph. The demolition of the gates around 1917 is traditional and no demolition order was located. The coordinate is the Plaza Italia entrance, distinct from the park pin used for the competition stop.
stops.campa: On the eleventh of November the park opens: twenty-five hectares of woods and lakes, a rose garden, a gazebo. His gates stand at the Plaza Italia end, monumental, with his avenue running from them into the trees. Porteños call them the Portones de Palermo and go on using the name for the whole neighbourhood long after the gates themselves come down, some time around 1917. What is left of them is a handful of photographs. No demolition order has been found, and no account says who ordered it.
suggested_refs: Photographs of the Portones de Palermo, Wikimedia Commons, Category:Jules Dormal
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: The port warehouses, the Sociedad Estímulo founded
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day. The legislative report says only 'Fue socio fundador de la Sociedad de Estímulo de las Bellas Artes' with no year; es.wikipedia's Sociedad Estímulo de Bellas Artes gives 23 October 1876 and lists 'el arquitecto Julio Dormal' among the founders, and angel_della_valle.journey.json carries the same date and roster independently. The location in Sívori family warehouse space near the port comes from hilariobooks.com, which gives no street number; the coordinate is approximate for the port district.
stops.campa: On the twenty-third of October a painters' association is founded in warehouse space belonging to the Sívori family business, down near the port. Eduardo Sívori and his brother Alejandro; Juan Camaña, who takes the chair; Eduardo Schiaffino; Santiago Vaca Guzmán; Alfred Paris; Carlos Gutiérrez; Giuseppe Agujari; and the architect Julio Dormal. The Sociedad Estímulo de Bellas Artes will be the first body in the country that teaches Argentines to paint. He is thirty and has built almost nothing yet.
suggested_refs: Founding minutes of the Sociedad Estímulo de Bellas Artes, 23 October 1876

stops.name: Buenos Aires Cathedral, the setting for San Martín
stops.date_confidence: Contested, and the contradiction is left standing. The legislative report says 'Fue responsable del Monumento a San Martín que se encuentra en la Catedral de Buenos Aires' and the Buenos Aires city heritage page lists the mausoleum among his works, but neither says what 'responsable' covers. es.wikipedia's Catedral Metropolitana credits the ensemble solely to Albert-Ernest Carrier-Belleuse and does not mention Dormal at all. 1880 is the year the remains were installed, not necessarily a date of Dormal's work. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus cathedral pin in san_martin.journey.json.
stops.campa: The remains of José de San Martín come home from Boulogne in 1880 and are set in the right nave of the cathedral, under a marble ensemble by the French sculptor Albert-Ernest Carrier-Belleuse. Two Argentine government sources make Dormal responsible for the monument. Neither of them says what responsible means, and the Spanish encyclopedia of the cathedral names Carrier-Belleuse alone. The likeliest division of the work, and it is only likely, gives Dormal the architectural enclosure and the sculptor everything standing inside it.
suggested_refs: Contracts and drawings for the 1880 installation of the San Martín mausoleum, Buenos Aires Cathedral, not located
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the plaster head of Sívori
stops.date_confidence: The bust is attested and signed; the year is not. hilariobooks.com, fetched, says the bust was 'realizado y firmado por Jules Dormal', was preserved by descendants of Dr. Luis Govi, was restored at the TAREA workshop of the Universidad de San Martín, and stood at the entrance of the 2023 MNBA exhibition. It supplies no date, and an earlier working draft rendered the year as '[1881]' in brackets, which is a tell that it was supplied rather than read. 1881 here orders the segment and nothing more. The studio where he modelled it is unrecorded; the coordinate is the general city pin.
stops.campa: He models a portrait head of the painter Eduardo Sívori in plaster and signs it. What the record carries is the signature, not a year, whatever the catalogues have since supplied. It is the one object anywhere that shows the architect working clay with his hands. The head stays with descendants of Dr. Luis Govi for a century, goes to the TAREA workshop of the Universidad de San Martín to be restored, and stands at the entrance of the 2023 Sívori exhibition at the Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes.
suggested_refs: The plaster bust of Eduardo Sívori by Jules Dormal, restored at TAREA/UNSAM, shown at the MNBA in 2023

segments.name: The Province Builds Itself a Capital

stops.name: La Plata, the cornerstone of the Government House
stops.date_confidence: Attested. es.wikipedia's Casa de Gobierno de la Provincia de Buenos Aires gives the cornerstone as 27 November 1882 and names Dormal as directing architect; the national monument decree, quoted in pedro_benoit.journey.json, places the plans with the Architecture Section of the provincial Department of Engineers under Benoit and adds an Italian architect, Luis Baldi, whom the encyclopedias omit. argentina.gob.ar confirms José Porret as master builder from 1882. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus La Plata Government House pin.
stops.campa: Eight days after the new provincial capital is founded, the stone of its Government House goes into the ground. The plans come from the Architecture Section of the provincial Department of Engineers, under Pedro Benoit, who has laid out the whole city on its diagonal grid. The decree that will one day make the building a national monument puts an Italian, Luis Baldi, beside Benoit on the drawings, and the encyclopedias that name Dormal omit Baldi altogether. The facades and the interiors are Dormal's, and so is the direction of the works.
stops.quote: En el año 1882, el PODER EJECUTIVO dispone que el DEPARTAMENTO DE INGENIEROS PROVINCIAL, proyecte los planos del edificio, quedando esto a cargo de la Sección Arquitectura dirigida por el arquitecto Pedro BENOIT.
stops.quote_source: Argentina, national historic-monument decree text for the La Plata Government Palace (norma-304920)
suggested_refs: The national monument decree for the Casa de Gobierno de La Plata, norma-304920

stops.name: Buenos Aires, ten founders or nine
stops.date_confidence: The founding date, 18 March 1886, is firm on both sides. Dormal's presence is not. The legislative report says 'Fue uno de los diez miembros fundadores... junto a Ernesto Bunge y Juan Antonio Buschiazzo'; hilariobooks.com repeats that he was a founder. But juan_antonio_buschiazzo.journey.json names nine founders from an independent roster and Dormal is not among them, and the legislative report's own enumeration likewise runs to nine names without his. The contradiction is real and is left unresolved. The founding venue is unknown; the coordinate is the general city pin.
stops.campa: Architects meet in Buenos Aires on the eighteenth of March to found the Sociedad Central de Arquitectos, the body that will put a border around the profession and decide who is inside it. Ernesto Bunge is there. Juan Antonio Buschiazzo is there. Whether Dormal is there is a genuine question, and it does not resolve: the provincial heritage report calls him one of the ten founders, while every surviving roster of that meeting, including the one Buschiazzo's own record carries, lists nine men and none of them is Dormal.
suggested_refs: Founding act of the Sociedad Central de Arquitectos, 18 March 1886, with its signatory list
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: Avenida Corrientes 860, the Ópera made French
stops.date_confidence: Attested by argentina.gob.ar's monument page for the Cine-Teatro Ópera, which dates the original theatre to 1872, names Émile Landois as its architect, and confirms Dormal's 1888 modification giving it a 'suntuosa imagen Beaux-Arts', with demolition in 1935 and Alberto Bourdon's replacement reopened 7 August 1936. Two errors in the legislative report are corrected here: it dates the original to 1871 and spells the entrepreneur 'Antonio Petalardo' for Pestalardo. No month is given for the 1888 work.
stops.campa: The Teatro de la Ópera on Corrientes, built in 1872 for the entrepreneur Antonio Pestalardo to a design by Émile Landois, is handed to Dormal to remodel. He gives it what the monument register calls a suntuosa imagen Beaux-Arts: French inside and out, gilded, heavy, costly. Porteño audiences know the house in that form for forty-seven years. In 1935 it comes down. Alberto Bourdon puts a cinema on the site and opens it on the seventh of August 1936, and the address stays the same.
suggested_refs: Photographs of the Teatro de la Ópera c. 1890, Wikimedia Commons, Category:Jules Dormal
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: Hipódromo de Palermo, the attribution nobody can date
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The Buenos Aires city heritage page for Florida 466 lists 'the Argentine Hippodrome in Palermo' among Dormal's works, and the legislative report says he built there 'con procedimientos novedosos para su época'. Neither gives a date and no permit or drawing has been produced. The city tourism page on the hippodrome, covering its whole history from 1883, does not mention him at all. The present grandstand is Louis Faure-Dujarric's of 1908 and does not conflict with earlier work. 1890 orders the segment. Coordinate corrected to Nominatim's Av. del Libertador 4101, -34.56640, -58.42573.
stops.campa: Out at Palermo, on the flat ground beyond the park he gated, the Jockey Club's racecourse is built up, and two Argentine government sources put Dormal's name on it, one of them describing methods novel for their time. What he built there and in what year is fixed by no permit anyone has produced, and a city tourism page that runs through the course's entire history does not name him once. The grandstand standing today is Louis Faure-Dujarric's, from 1908.
suggested_refs: Jockey Club building records for the Hipódromo Argentino de Palermo, 1880s-1900s
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: La Plata, the Government House opened
stops.date_confidence: Two state sources, three years apart, about one building. es.wikipedia gives construction 1883-1892 with inauguration in 1892; argentina.gob.ar's monument page says the Bertelli firm continued the work from 1883 to 1892 'which concluded in 1895'. Both are printed by Argentine authority and neither is preferred here. The best formulation is cornerstone 27 November 1882, inauguration 1892, works fully concluded 1895. No inauguration day or month was located. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus La Plata Government House pin.
stops.campa: Ten years of building: José Porret the master builder from 1882, the firm of Santiago Bertelli y Cía from 1883 to 1892, and Dormal over all of it. The Government House of the province of Buenos Aires opens in 1892, French Renaissance in brick and stone, facing Plaza San Martín across the block bounded by calles 5, 6, 51 and 53. The federal monument register says the works were not fully concluded until 1895. Two arms of the same state print the two dates and neither corrects the other.
suggested_refs: The Casa de Gobierno de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, La Plata, and the Dormal facades

segments.name: The Chair, the Society, the Commission

stops.name: Universidad de Buenos Aires, the chair of architecture
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. Hodge (1979), summarised via Cambridge Core, says he 'served as Professor of Architecture at the University of Buenos Aires until his death'. No appointment record, faculty minute or course listing was located, and the specific building the architecture programme occupied in this period is unclear; the coordinate approximates the historic university precinct. The start year is not attested and 1901 orders the segment only.
stops.campa: He is made professor of architecture at the University of Buenos Aires and holds the chair, by Hodge's account, until he dies. No appointment record has surfaced, no faculty minute, no course listing, and which building the school occupies in these first years is not fixed in anything reachable. The Belgian who came out to boil beef teaches Argentines what a building is, and holds the post through the Colón, the Congreso and the station at Mar del Plata. The men who will design the centenary city sit in front of him.
suggested_refs: Faculty appointment records, Universidad de Buenos Aires school of architecture, c. 1901-1924
sources: Robert Hodge, 'The Construction of the Teatro Colón', The Americas (1979), via Cambridge Core

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the society put back on its feet
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction, and the joint role is unconfirmed. alejandro_christophersen.journey.json names Christophersen as 'one of the refounders of the Sociedad Central de Arquitectos' around 1901 and does not name Dormal as co-convener; the dossier tradition has the two of them convening the reconstitution together. No minute of the refounding was located. The date orders the segment. The venue is unknown and the coordinate is the general city pin.
stops.campa: The Sociedad Central has gone quiet and is put back on its feet at the turn of the century. Alejandro Christophersen is named among its refounders in every account: Norwegian by descent, Belgian-connected, Paris-finished, a man formed the same way Dormal was formed and twenty years younger. The tradition has the two of them convening the reconstitution between them. Christophersen's own record names him among the refounders and does not name Dormal. No minute of the meeting has been found.
suggested_refs: Minutes of the reconstitution of the Sociedad Central de Arquitectos, c. 1901-1902
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: Municipalidad, the commission that buys the city its art
stops.date_confidence: Unconfirmed. The claim that Dormal sat on a municipal art-acquisition commission under intendente Alberto Casares with Carlos Thays, Eduardo Schiaffino and Ernesto de la Cárcova comes from the provincial legislative compilation. The one scholarly article that might have confirmed it, 'Fragmentos de admiración' at sedici.unlp.edu.ar, exceeded fetchable size and could not be read. No minutes of the commission were located. The coordinate is the old municipal seat near Plaza de Mayo; the date orders the segment.
stops.campa: Under the intendente Alberto Casares the city sets up a commission to buy art for Buenos Aires, and Dormal is reported sitting on it beside Carlos Thays, who is at that moment remaking the Palermo woods thirty years after Dormal gated them, beside Eduardo Schiaffino from the Sociedad Estímulo, and beside Ernesto de la Cárcova. Four men deciding what a capital will be made to look at. No minute of any of their meetings has come to light, and the one study that might have settled the roster could not be opened.
suggested_refs: 'Fragmentos de admiración', sedici.unlp.edu.ar, on the Buenos Aires municipal art-acquisition commission
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: Arenales y Maipú, the Ortiz Basualdo house
stops.date_confidence: Completion in 1904 is attested by the FADU-UBA inventory at isu.fadu.uba.ar, which lists the Palacio Ortiz Basualdo under Dormal Godet and places it in Barrio Norte. The location is corrected: the legislative report puts it precisely at 'Arenales y Maipú', roughly -34.5940, -58.3823, and a working value of -34.5951, -58.3760 placed it facing Plaza San Martín about 590 m east. Beware conflation with the other Palacio Ortiz Basualdo, the French embassy at Cerrito 1399, which is Pablo Pater's and not Dormal's. Demolished after 1969; no demolition permit located.
stops.campa: At Arenales and Maipú he finishes a small palace for Inés Ortiz Basualdo de Peña, one of the French townhouses Barrio Norte fills with in the years before the centenary: compact, stone, a courtyard behind. It is demolished. The name attaches afterwards to a different building altogether, the Ortiz Basualdo palace on Cerrito that houses the French embassy, which is Pablo Pater's work and never was his. Confusing the two is the commonest error in the whole Dormal catalogue.
suggested_refs: Instituto de Arte Americano, FADU-UBA, inventory entry for Palacio Ortiz Basualdo (Dormal Godet)
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: Buenos Aires, first prize for facades
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the legislative report ('Su genialidad le mereció recibir el primer premio de fachadas de Buenos Aires en 1905') and corroborated by Hodge, who says the Ortiz Basualdo townhouse 'won the annual architectural award in 1905'. The two accounts disagree over whether the prize was for one house or several; the citation itself has not been located. No month is on record and the coordinate is the general city pin, the award ceremony's venue being unknown.
stops.campa: The city awards him first prize for building facades. The legislative report says the prize covered several private residences; Hodge says it was the Ortiz Basualdo townhouse that won it. The citation itself has not been found, so which is right is anybody's guess. He is fifty-nine. In the same twelvemonth the Teatro Colón and the Palace of Congress both come onto his desk, half built, out of money, and drawn by two men who are dead. He takes both of them on.
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires municipal facade prize records for 1905
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8
Robert Hodge, 'The Construction of the Teatro Colón', The Americas (1979)

stops.name: Teatro Colón, the third architect
stops.date_confidence: Attested. es.wikipedia's Historia del Teatro Colón puts Dormal's assumption of the direction in February 1905 following Meano's death; no day is given. Meano was shot on 1 June 1904 at the age of forty-four, per the theatre's institutional history. Tamburini won the bid in 1889 and laid the stone on 25 May 1890, and francesco_tamburini.journey.json corrects the common Argentine claim that he died the same year: en.wikipedia and it.wikipedia both put his death in 1891. His birth year is itself contested, 1846 against 1848, so the 'aged 44' figure that seeds the architects'-curse legend is not securely establishable. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Teatro Colón pin.
stops.campa: Francesco Tamburini won the Colón by public bid in 1889 and laid its stone on the twenty-fifth of May 1890, and died the year after. Vittorio Meano carried the drawings on and was shot dead in 1904. Juan Antonio Buschiazzo had campaigned in 1899 to have the half-built walls pulled down, and fifteen years after the first stone they are standing yet. In February 1905 the municipality hands the theatre to Dormal: honorary director, third architect, fifty-nine years old, the only one of the three who will be alive on the opening night.
suggested_refs: Municipal decree appointing Dormal honorary director of the Teatro Colón works, February 1905

stops.name: Teatro Colón, the marquee over Libertad
stops.date_confidence: Attested in substance, not in month. es.wikipedia's Historia del Teatro Colón describes the elimination of rooms, the addition of 'la gran marquesina vidriada' over Calle Libertad, and Dormal's serious disagreements with Meano's work 'especialmente en materia de seguridad', without dating any of them beyond the 1905-1907 window. September 1905 orders the segment. The 1903 municipal inspection commission verdict is quoted from Telémaco Susini via Shmidt, carried in francesco_tamburini.journey.json. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Teatro Colón pin.
stops.campa: He goes through Meano's building and does not like what he finds. Rooms are eliminated. Over Calle Libertad he hangs a great glazed marquee of iron and glass, the most visible single thing on the theatre that is his and not theirs. The disagreements he records with his predecessor are about safety. A municipal inspection commission had said the same in 1903 and said it harder, calling the half-built house nothing but the product of an enterprise of profit and speculation with almost no account taken of the safety of the audience.
stops.quote: el teatro Colón... debe ser un teatro modelo porque es un edificio público, oficial, que cuesta varios millones [y en cambio] no ha sido otra cosa en su origen que el producto de una empresa de lucro y de especulación en que poco se ha tenido absolutamente en cuenta la seguridad de los concurrentes
stops.quote_source: Municipal inspection commission report, quoted by Telémaco Susini, 'Defectos del nuevo edificio del Teatro Colón', Arquitectura N.6, July 1904, p.59
suggested_refs: The glazed marquee over Calle Libertad, Teatro Colón

stops.name: Palacio del Congreso, inaugurated unfinished
stops.date_confidence: Inauguration attested to the day by es.wikipedia's Palacio del Congreso de la Nación Argentina: 'El Palacio fue inaugurado el 12 de mayo de 1906', with the works 'completamente finalizadas recién en 1946, con el revestimiento en piedra de la rotonda sobre la calle Combate de los Pozos'. argentina.gob.ar corroborates 1906 and 1946 and names Dormal as the man who completed the project after Meano. The construction start is contested: es.wikipedia says August 1897, the legislative report says 1898. Both are carried.
stops.campa: The Palace of Congress opens on the twelfth of May, Meano's competition design of 1895 carried up to its dome by the man who took the work over after the murder. Dormal keeps his predecessor's scheme and puts his own decorative hand on it inside and out. The building is not finished. The stone facing of the rotunda over Combate de los Pozos will not be laid until 1946, forty years on and twenty-two years after Dormal is dead. Whether the works began in August 1897 or in 1898 the sources do not agree.
suggested_refs: The dome of the Palacio del Congreso and Dormal's decorative programme
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: Teatro Colón, the orchestra floor pulled down
stops.date_confidence: Attested in substance, not in month. es.wikipedia's Historia del Teatro Colón records that Dormal had the mobile orchestra platform demolished and rebuilt at the contracting firm's expense; August 1906 orders the segment. The quote is Amalia Pellizzari, granddaughter of the contractor Francisco Pellizzari, from a family chronicle relayed by that article: a chronicler's account of Dormal's stated view, not his own words, and the family-history strand is a plausible technical core rather than a proven one. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Teatro Colón pin.
stops.campa: He orders the mobile floor of the orchestra pit demolished and rebuilt, and charges the whole cost to the contractors, Pellizzari y Armellini, who built it. The granddaughter of one of them will write later that Dormal would sooner have knocked the entire theatre down and started over, as some members of the municipal commission and the engineer Buschiazzo had proposed back in 1900, and that by 1906 this was no longer a thing anyone could do. The theatre was almost finished.
stops.quote: Dormal hubiese querido demoler todo y comenzar la construcción desde cero, como habían propuesto alguna vez ciertos miembros de la Comisión Municipal y el ing. Juan A. Buschiazzo en el año 1900. Pero esto es ya imposible. El teatro está casi terminado.
stops.quote_source: Amalia Pellizzari, family chronicle, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Historia del Teatro Colón'
suggested_refs: The Pellizzari family chronicle of the Teatro Colón works

stops.name: Teatro Colón, Armellini walks off the job
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day. es.wikipedia's Historia del Teatro Colón gives 11 de abril de 1907 for Ítalo Armellini's withdrawal from the contracting firm 'con su sistema nervioso agotado', leaving Francisco Pellizzari to continue alone, and attributes the conflict to the strictness of Dormal's construction requirements. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Teatro Colón pin.
stops.campa: On the eleventh of April Ítalo Armellini withdraws from the contracting firm with his nervous system exhausted, in the phrase the record keeps, and Francisco Pellizzari goes on alone. The requirements Dormal has been imposing are stricter than the contract anticipated and the money to meet them is not there. Nothing the architect says about it is written down, and the only account of the quarrel comes from the other contractor's family. The name on the contract has read Pellizzari y Armellini. From this day it reads Pellizzari.
suggested_refs: The Pellizzari y Armellini contract for the Teatro Colón works

stops.name: Teatro Colón, the structure closed
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by es.wikipedia's Historia del Teatro Colón, which gives the completion of the structure as 28 February 1908. The stylistic judgement quoted here is the legislative report's, and its exact wording is corrected: the PDF reads 'toda su GENEROSIDAD artística y su influencia estilística BORBÓNICA', not the 'genialidad artística' that circulates. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Teatro Colón pin.
stops.campa: The structure is closed on the twenty-eighth of February, eighteen years and nine months after the first stone. The Salón Dorado is not finished, not all the exterior iron and glass is hung, and the decoration is still going in. Three architects have held these drawings and two of them are dead. What the third has principally left on the house is inside it, and the provincial heritage report, describing that interior, credits him with his artistic generosity and his Bourbon stylistic influence.
stops.quote: Fue el último de los tres arquitectos que intervino en su construcción y lo hizo principalmente en los interiores, donde puso en evidencia toda su generosidad artística y su influencia estilística borbónica.
stops.quote_source: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8
suggested_refs: The Dormal interiors of the Teatro Colón
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: Teatro Colón, opened with Aida
stops.date_confidence: Attested. es.wikipedia's Historia del Teatro Colón and teatrocolon.org.ar both give 25 May 1908 and Verdi's Aida, and the theatre's own history records that sections including the Salón Dorado remained unfinished at the opening. The date is eighteen years to the day from Tamburini's cornerstone of 25 May 1890, both dates being the national holiday. Dormal's presence in the house on the night is not separately documented, though he was its acting director. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Teatro Colón pin.
stops.campa: Aida, on the twenty-fifth of May, eighteen years to the day since the stone went down. The horseshoe the Italians drew, the French finish the Belgian put on it, the Salón Dorado still bare behind the audience. The acoustics that will make the house famous across the world were not his design and he never claims them. Tamburini did not live to hear a note in it and neither did Meano. Dormal is sixty-two, and he has held these drawings for three years and three months.
suggested_refs: The inauguration of the Teatro Colón, 25 May 1908

stops.name: Teatro Colón, sat for Jules Lagae
stops.date_confidence: Attested by weboeba.com's Dormal entry, which gives the whole chain: a bronze bust forty centimetres high modelled by Jules Lagae in 1909, donated to the Teatro Colón by the sculptor's son, formalised by 'Decreto - Ordenanza n.o 9966 del 12 de agosto de 1962', inaugurated in September 1962 in the foyer entered from Calle Libertad. An AGORHA/INHA record that might document the modelling returned 403 and es.wikipedia is silent on the bust; neither silence is evidence against it. Where Lagae modelled him, and whether from life, is not stated. The stop sits at the building the bronze ends up in.
stops.campa: The Belgian sculptor Jules Lagae models him in 1909, a bronze head forty centimetres high, made while the sitter is alive and at the top of what he has done. Where the modelling happens the record does not say. Long afterwards the sculptor's son gives the bust to the Teatro Colón; a municipal decree-ordinance of the twelfth of August 1962 formalises the gift, and that September it is set up in the foyer entered from Calle Libertad, under his own marquee, with four lines cut on the plaque.
stops.quote: JULIO DORMAL (1846-1924) ARQUITECTO - INGENIERO / JULES LAGAE / 1909
stops.quote_source: Bronze plaque, Teatro Colón foyer, installed 1962 under Buenos Aires Decree-Ordinance no. 9966 of 12 August 1962; transcribed at weboeba.com
suggested_refs: The Lagae bust of Julio Dormal, foyer of the Teatro Colón; Decreto-Ordenanza 9966 of 12 August 1962

segments.name: The Coast, the Council, and the Rented City

stops.name: Mar del Plata, the terminus drawn as an L
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the provincial legislative heritage report, downloaded and parsed with pypdf: 'El edificio, en forma de "L", fue proyectado y dirigido por el arquitecto belga Jules Dormal', occupying the block bounded by Alberti, Sarmiento, Garay and Las Heras, its main entrance 'solo siete cuadras de la plaza Colón'. The clock tower on the Sarmiento axis was drawn and not built. Coordinate corrected: Nominatim resolves Alberti 1600 to -38.01191, -57.54272, in the neighbourhood still called Vieja Terminal; a working value of -38.0055, -57.5426 sat about 700 m north at Plaza Colón latitude.
stops.campa: The Ferrocarril Sud brings its line into Mar del Plata and Dormal draws the terminus: an L on the block bounded by Alberti, Sarmiento, Garay and Las Heras, seven blocks up from Plaza Colón. Central hall, a café, waiting rooms, ticket offices, and above them the offices and the stationmaster's flat. On the Sarmiento front his drawing puts a clock tower on the axis. What gets built is smaller than what he drew and there is no tower on it. He directs the works himself, in the report's phrase: proyectado y dirigido.
suggested_refs: Original Ferrocarril Sud drawings for the Estación Mar del Plata Sud
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), Art. 1 and p.4

stops.name: Mar del Plata, the first train to the platforms
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by the legislative report: 'El 1 de diciembre de 1910 corrió el primer tren de pasajeros hasta los recién terminados andenes', with a wooden shed serving as the provisional station. The attribution of the old wooden rambla at Playa Bristol to Dormal is a separate matter and is left flagged: the same report discusses the 'rambla afrancesada' repeatedly, notes its architecture was 'muy similar a la de esta Estación', and never once names him as its author, which from a report cataloguing his works is meaningful negative evidence.
stops.campa: On the first of December the first passenger train runs up to the platforms, which are finished, and halts beside a wooden shed, which is the station for now. The season is starting and the coast will not wait for masonry. Bathers come down from Buenos Aires past the scaffolding to the beach and to the old wooden rambla on Playa Bristol, that French-looking boardwalk which more than one catalogue hands to Dormal and which this very report on his own station never says is his.
suggested_refs: Photographs of the provisional wooden station at Mar del Plata Sud, summer 1910-1911
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.4

stops.name: Mar del Plata, the definitive station opened
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by the legislative report: 'hasta la inauguración del edificio definitivo, realizada el 1 de diciembre de 1911'. The same report supplies the closing chronology: last season 1947-1948, removal of the service approved 1950, rails lifted 1951, bus terminal thereafter until 2009. An es.wikipedia article on the Estación Mar del Plata Sud and a Ferrocarril Sud variant both returned 404 and could not be used.
stops.campa: A year to the day, the definitive building opens. It works as a railway station for thirty-seven more summers. The last season is 1947 to 1948; removal of the service is approved in 1950 and the rails come up in 1951. Buses move into the hall afterwards and stay there until 2009. The building is standing, and the report that sets all of this down is a bill drawn up to protect it. People who have never in their lives seen a train on that block still call the neighbourhood around it the Vieja Terminal.
suggested_refs: The Estación Mar del Plata Sud building, block of Alberti, Sarmiento, Garay and Las Heras
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), Art. 1 and p.4

stops.name: Concejo Deliberante, the councilman who is not a citizen
stops.date_confidence: The council service, 1910 to 1915, comes from the legislative report ('Se desempeñó también como concejal de la ciudad de Buenos Aires entre 1910 y 1915'). Attempted independent verification of the underlying PDF over the open web returned corrupted binary; the report was later parsed successfully with pypdf from a local download. The specific proposals attributed to him, widening Corrientes and permitting taller buildings, are reconstruction and the council's own minutes for these years were not consulted. 1912 orders the segment. The coordinate is the council's general seat near Plaza de Mayo.
stops.campa: He sits on the city council of Buenos Aires from 1910 to 1915, a Belgian who never naturalised, voting on the building code of a city he has been putting up for forty years. He is reported to have pressed for the widening of Corrientes and for permission to build taller. That report rests on a provincial legislative compilation, and the council's own minutes for those five years have not been read by anyone writing about him. What he actually voted for is a gap.
suggested_refs: Actas del Concejo Deliberante de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, 1910-1915
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: Florida 466, the rental building for the Peñas
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the Buenos Aires city heritage page for Florida 466, which names Julio Dormal as architect and says the building 'fue inaugurado en 1913'. No month is given. Coordinate corrected: Nominatim resolves Florida 466, San Nicolás, to -34.60265, -58.37531, and a working value of -34.5996, -58.3746 landed near Plaza San Martín, about 340 m off. The neighbouring Peña-Blaye residence, later the Sociedad Rural Argentina, is attributed to him by the Wikimedia Commons category but by no heritage record fetched here, and its street number and date are unconfirmed.
stops.campa: At Florida 466 he raises a rental building for the Peña family, inaugurated in 1913: flats above, commerce on the ground floor, on the street where Buenos Aires does its walking. Next door stands the Peña-Blaye residence, also given to him, which the Sociedad Rural Argentina takes over. Two Dormal fronts in a row, if the second one is his: that attribution rests on a photograph caption, and no heritage record carries it. Its street number and its date are unconfirmed as well.
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires city heritage record for Florida 466; Wikimedia Commons, 'Sociedad Rural, Calle Florida, Buenos Aires.jpg'

stops.name: Florida 468, the Richmond opens downstairs
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by es.wikipedia's Confitería Richmond, which gives 17 November 1917 and the address Florida 468, 'en la planta baja de un edificio diseñado por el arquitecto belga Jules Dormal junto a la Residencia Peña'; the city heritage page confirms 1917 and the Grupo de Florida association. Note the two-number discrepancy: the building is catalogued at 466, the confitería at 468. Coordinate as corrected for Florida 466 above. Dormal's own presence in the café is not documented.
stops.campa: On the seventeenth of November a confitería opens on the ground floor at Florida 468, in his building. It is called the Richmond, and the upper class of Buenos Aires makes a habit of it. Within a few years the writers have the back tables: Ricardo Güiraldes, Oliverio Girondo, Jorge Luis Borges and the rest of what the country will call the Grupo de Florida, arguing about Martín Fierro under his ceiling. He is seventy-one and lives eight blocks away. Nobody records whether he ever went in.
suggested_refs: The Confitería Richmond, Florida 468, and the Grupo de Florida

stops.name: Arroyo 1130, called in over another man's staircase
stops.date_confidence: Attested by argentina.gob.ar's Palacio Pereda page, which has Louis Martin creating the initial Beaux-Arts design and 'Julio Dormal made revisions at the request of owner Celedonio Pereda'; es.wikipedia's Palacio Pereda dates the replacement to 1919, with the interior and staircase design as the cause, and work running 1920-1936. The legislative report's 'Celestino Pereda' is the source's own error. Its 'Desde 1944' for the Brazilian residence is also corrected: the property passed to Brazil after Pereda's death in 1945. Coordinate corrected to Arroyo 1130, -34.591755, -58.383447; a working value put it at Cerrito 1350, nearly a kilometre west.
stops.campa: Celedonio Pereda has a French architect, Louis Martin, and does not like what Martin has done with the interior and the staircase, and in 1919 he sends for Dormal. The legislative report that lists the commission calls the client Celestino, which was never his name. The house on Arroyo runs on from 1920 to 1936. Josep Maria Sert paints its ceilings in 1932, eight years after Dormal is in the ground. When Pereda dies in 1945 his heirs trade the palace to Brazil against the old embassy on Callao, and the Brazilian ambassador lives in it still.
suggested_refs: The Palacio Pereda, Arroyo 1130, residence of the ambassador of Brazil
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

segments.name: The House on Plaza San Martín

stops.name: San Martín 1137, the front he puts on himself
stops.date_confidence: Date unresolved and both years are carried: infobae (3 November 2024) gives 1920, other sources give 1913, and the arquitectos-franceses blog that describes the building in most detail gives no construction year at all. The architectural description is confirmed verbatim by that blog: 'cuatro largas columnas corintias de fuste liso', 'cuatro bajorrelieves con motivos diferentes donde los protagonistas son querubines', 'Dos pares de columnas... de orden jónico', 'un frontis triangular'. The structural figures come from a 2024 sale listing and are advertised rather than surveyed. Coordinate corrected to Nominatim's San Martín 1137, -34.59449, -58.37432; the geography and afterlife working values disagreed with each other by about 200 m and neither was right.
stops.campa: On the south side of Plaza San Martín, at San Martín 1137, he builds for himself: six levels over a basement, some thirty rooms, seventeen hundred square metres on a lot of three hundred and fifteen. Four Corinthian columns with smooth shafts, two pairs of Ionic ones, four relief panels with cherubs in them, a triangular pediment, a carriage entrance. Fifty years of devices he has put on other men's houses, all of it loaded onto one narrow front. Whether he builds it in 1913 or in 1920 the record will not settle.
suggested_refs: San Martín 1137, Buenos Aires, protected under city heritage code APH 38
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.8

stops.name: San Martín 1137, the will written by hand
stops.date_confidence: The 1922 handwritten will is attested by his descendant Magdalena Paz Miguens at the 2024 centenary, reported by fmradiocultura.com.ar, which says he wrote it in perfect Spanish entirely in his own hand and signed it Julio Dormal. The text has never been published and was not seen. No day or month is given. The family counts are also from that report: three marriages, ten children, six grandchildren, thirty great-grandchildren, over 250 great-great-grandchildren. The legislative report gives two marriages, Amalia Peña then Elina Sosa Díaz, and three children, Carmen, Julia and Carlos. The two counts are irreconcilable as they stand and both are carried. The place of writing is assumed to be his house.
stops.campa: In 1922, two years before he dies, he writes his will out by hand, in Spanish, and signs it Julio Dormal. The family holds it and has never published a line of it. How large that family is depends on who is counting. The provincial heritage report gives him two marriages, to Amalia Peña and then, widowed, to Elina Sosa Díaz of a prominent Uruguayan house, and three children: Carmen, Julia, Carlos. His descendants, gathered a century later, count three marriages and ten children and more than two hundred and fifty great-great-grandchildren.
stops.quote: Conservamos en nuestra familia el testamento de este gran arquitecto escrito en 1922, dos años antes de su muerte.
stops.quote_source: Magdalena Paz Miguens, remarks at the centenary homage to Dormal, Teatro Colón, 21 August 2024, reported by fmradiocultura.com.ar
suggested_refs: The unpublished holograph will of Jules Dormal, 1922, in family hands
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), pp.8-9

stops.name: San Martín 1137, the death in his own house
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day and place by the arquitectos-franceses blog, whose caption on the building reads 'El arquitecto Jules Dormal falleció aquí el 22 de Marzo de 1924', and by the legislative report, p.9: 'Murió en Buenos Aires el 22 de marzo de 1924'. Born in 1846 with no day recorded, he is seventy-seven or seventy-eight. Coordinate as corrected for San Martín 1137.
stops.campa: He dies in the house on Plaza San Martín on the twenty-second of March, seventy-seven years old or seventy-eight, no birth day being on record. He has lived in Argentina fifty-four years without taking its citizenship. The three buildings his name is best known for were every one of them begun by another man. Outside in the country stand a provincial parliament, a national congress, an opera house, a racecourse, a rental block on Florida and a railway terminus on the sea. The office he opened in 1870 closes with him.
suggested_refs: The 2010 architectural survey caption at San Martín 1137 recording the death
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.9

stops.name: Cementerio de la Recoleta, the vault that is no longer there
stops.date_confidence: Burial at Recoleta is attested by the legislative report, which says he was buried 'en su bóveda en la Recoleta', and by recoletacemetery.com, which specifies the mausoleum of his second wife, Elena or Elina Sosa Díaz. The exhumation chain is tagged reconstruction by that source itself: cemetery records showing cremation in 1989 and remains 'likely placed inside the Dolmas Arévalo vault, though the reason remains undocumented', with neither tomb standing today. No official cemetery response was obtained. The burial day is not recorded and 24 March orders it. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Recoleta pin in juan_antonio_buschiazzo.journey.json; pedro_benoit.journey.json carries -34.5878, -58.3932 for the same cemetery and the divergence is noted, not resolved.
stops.campa: He is buried in Recoleta, in the vault of his second wife's family, a few paces inside the gate Juan Antonio Buschiazzo built and within walls that already hold Pedro Benoit. The cemetery's own records, as read by a specialist who has been through them, show the remains cremated in 1989 and probably moved to a vault called Dolmas Arévalo, for a reason nobody wrote down. Neither the Sosa Díaz tomb nor the Dolmas Arévalo vault exists at Recoleta now. Where he is, nobody can say.
suggested_refs: Cementerio de la Recoleta administrative records for the Sosa Díaz and Dolmas Arévalo vaults
sources: Honorable Cámara de Diputados de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, expte. 2680/09-10 (PDF), p.9
